A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 17-page versions of the same FUEL paper. The text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered figures.

before.justification: Sections 4–6 and Appendices C–E report original Qwen2.5 and Llama2 serving experiments, including latency, output quality, benchmark scores, and modeled carbon emissions.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and revises the reported Arena Hard quality distributions in Figure 24.

M1.justification: The four-step FUEL procedure, functional-unit criteria, reward-based Qscore, profiling, and carbon calculations are unchanged. Explicitly naming Skywork clarifies the reward model already cited in v1.

E1.justification: Both evaluate NewsQA summarization, Arena Hard instruction following, HumanEval code generation, and the same six quality benchmarks in Table 2. The new RewardBench citation does not introduce an evaluation.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same Qwen and Llama model sizes, FP16/AWQ/W8A8 variants, and L40/H100 hardware comparisons. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Table 1 revises the stated H100 GPU TDP from 350 W to 700 W. This changes a reported hardware specification without establishing a changed power cap or rerun. The single-GPU design, QPS ranges, and latency thresholds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2's analysis of quality differences across model sizes receives a corrected supporting plot: Figure 24 replaces duplicated HumanEval curves with distinct Arena Hard distributions. Other supplementary analyses and experimental sweeps are retained.

E5.justification: Both explicitly report single-run experiments and retain the same distribution-summary practices. No run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: V1's Arena Hard Figure 24 repeats the HumanEval plot in Figure 28. V2 replaces Figure 24, changing the reported cumulative Qscore curves, including the separation between Llama models. Tables 2–3 and all other matched experimental plots retain their results.

T1.justification: The FU-count definition and carbon-model equations, including Appendix B's manufacturing and packaging calculations, remain unchanged. Standardizing CO2-equivalent unit labels does not revise the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: Both retain the first FU-based evaluation-framework claim, the three case-study contributions, and the conditional findings about model size, quantization, and hardware. Abstract and introduction edits preserve their scientific scope.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly explains that fewer qualifying responses increase smaller models' carbon per FU. It expands the hardware interpretation to discuss throughput, memory capacity, and power consumption alongside embodied carbon, and softens reward-score agreement from 'most closely' to 'well.' The limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly identifies the pretrained Skywork reward model, revises the H100 TDP specification, and replaces Appendix A's anonymous repository pointer and README description with a named GitHub repository in the abstract. These are documentation and access-information changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds RewardBench (Lambert et al., 2024) to support reward-model selection and EnsembleCI (Yan et al., 2025) in the carbon-intensity discussion. The broader related-work coverage and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: The abstract and ethical statement are edited, selected explanations are expanded, acknowledgments are added, and Appendix A becomes 'Appendix Overview.' The main narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The NewsQA quality histogram moves from v1 Figure 21 in the appendix to v2 Figure 3 in the main text. Figure 24 is revised, including its Qwen axis range, and other figures and tables reflow. Most visual designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 fixes Figure 24's misleading duplication of HumanEval results and improves explanations of FU normalization and hardware trade-offs. Explicit evaluator identification and updated code-access information also improve usability. These are localized gains within otherwise stable evidence; a stale appendix locator for the moved Figure 3 remains in Section 4.1.
